note: X509 CRLs given as an OIDC private key whose nested encodings are corrupt at each level: X509CRLHolder reads with a lazily evaluating ASN1InputStream, so each definite-length SEQUENCE is a LazyEncodedSequence decoded only when a structure reads it, and its failure is an ASN1ParsingException (`malformed ASN.1: ...`) wrapped as malformed data; what no structure reads never fails. Record it on a freshly started oracle: once the JIT has compiled ASN1Sequence.getObjectAt, the oracle throws its ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException without a message (OmitStackTraceInFastThrow).

mask.regex: \{\s*"localizedMessage" : "Index \d+ out of bounds for length \d+",\s*"message" : "Index \d+ out of bounds for length \d+",\s*"stackTrace" : <frames>\s*\}
mask.reason: the oracle's JVM throws BouncyCastle's ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException with the JDK's message until its JIT compiles the throwing method, then a preallocated one without message or stack (OmitStackTraceInFastThrow): which one a step meets depends on JIT timing; ours is always the cold one
